title: Patatas Bravas
subtitle: Spanish fried potatoes with a spicy tomato sauce
excerpt: The most ordered tapa in Spain: cubes of potato fried until crisp in abundant olive oil, served with a fierce, smoky tomato sauce (salsa brava) made from tinned tomatoes, smoked paprika, and a kick of cayenne. Nothing complicated, everything correct.

recipe.sourceNotes: Patatas bravas (brave potatoes, referring to the spicy sauce) originated as a tapa in Madrid in the mid-twentieth century and became one of the definitive dishes of Spanish bar culture. The sauce varies significantly by region: the Madrid version (salsa brava) is a spicy, tomato-based red sauce; the Catalan version pairs the bravas sauce with aioli; some Barcelona versions use only the aioli. The potatoes must be cooked twice — first at a lower temperature to cook through, then at a higher temperature to achieve the crisp exterior. Fried in olive oil rather than sunflower oil, they develop a characteristic richness.

recipeTools.notes: A deep heavy pan for frying.

content.text: Dry the potato cubes very well after cutting: surface moisture will cause them to steam rather than fry and prevents a crisp exterior. Double-fry at 140 C then 190 C for the crispest result; a single fry at 180 C produces an acceptable alternative. The sauce is made separately and poured over at the last minute so the potatoes stay crisp.

items.preparation: cut into 3 cm cubes; dried thoroughly
for frying; or use vegetable oil

content.text: Make the sauce: cook the onion in a little oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, and cayenne and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Add the sherry vinegar and season with salt. Blend until smooth.

Heat the oil in a deep heavy pan to 140 C. Fry the potato cubes in batches for 8 minutes until cooked through but not coloured. Remove and drain on a rack. Increase the oil to 190 C and fry the potatoes again in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Season the hot potatoes with sea salt. Pile onto a plate, spoon the warm sauce generously over the top, and scatter with parsley. Serve immediately.
